name: Thalamic glutamatergic projection (thalamocortical relay) neuron
morphology_summary: Relay-like projection cells with soma-derived axon and few local collaterals; bushy and radiate dendritic patterns; core-like (low variability) vs matrix-like (higher variability, broad superficial-layer cortical projection, e.g. MD Calb1 neurons) axonal projection styles
ephys_summary: Not characterised directly in the report; genes on the main mediolateral transcriptional axis are enriched for ion channels and receptors, implying systematic variation in membrane/response properties across thalamus
subtypes_noted: Not a single uniform type: graded heterogeneity along a mediolateral (primary-secondary-tertiary) transcriptional axis repeated across sensory, motor and cognitive pathways (Phillips et al., 2017, 2019); within VL, Pvalb-selective, Tnnt1-selective and intermediate neurons coexist; projection-target-biased clusters by Epi-Retro-Seq (Zhou et al., 2023); ABC atlas class 18 TH Glut spans 58 subclasses/163 supertypes/563 clusters in the thalamic region (Turner et al., 2025); core vs matrix (Pvalb vs Calb1) styles (Zhao et al., 2026). PVT, ATN and dLGN relay neurons are treated as nucleus-specific members of this family

name: Paraventricular thalamic nucleus (PVT) glutamatergic projection neuron
morphology_summary: No sharply distinct somatodendritic morphologies among midline neurons; bushy-like and radiate-like dendrites; soma-derived axon with little local branching
ephys_summary: Calretinin (Calb2)-positive midline neurons are physiologically distinct from CR-negative neurons, with differential coupling to hippocampal network states (Lara-Vasquez et al., 2016)
subtypes_noted: Four continuous PVT types along the anterior-posterior axis with near non-overlapping aPVT/pPVT projections and an intermediate population (Shima et al., 2022); five molecularly distinct subtypes PVT1-5 arranged on combined AP/ML/DV gradients with differing cortical projection overlap (Gao et al., 2023); CR+ vs CR- midline populations (Lara-Vasquez et al., 2016). Human PVT-like ExN_CALB neurons (Nishioka et al., 2026)

name: Anterior thalamic nuclei (ATN) excitatory projection neuron
subtypes_noted: Three discrete excitatory clusters matching AD, AV and AM, each with graded variation along a dorsomedial-ventrolateral axis; AV shows spatially covarying protein products and long-range inputs (Kapustina et al., 2024); AV/AD clusters enriched for retrosplenial-projecting neurons (Zhou et al., 2023); AM contains discrete subdomains in THALMANAC (Turner et al., 2025). Specific markers not listed in the report

name: Dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus (dLGN) principal thalamocortical relay neuron
morphology_summary: Thalamocortical neurons with distinct morphologies across types (described across mammals); retina-recipient, projecting to primary visual cortex
ephys_summary: Not described for mouse in the report; types convey different aspects of visual information
subtypes_noted: Modest, gradient-like adult transcriptomic diversity in mouse along a core-shell axis: Pvalb-enriched core neurons (align with primate M/P) vs Calb1/Necab1-enriched shell neurons (align with primate koniocellular) (Bakken et al., 2021)

name: Dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus (dLGN) local GABAergic interneuron
morphology_summary: Local interneuron; no further detail in the report
subtypes_noted: Sparse population; the report notes the quotes do not detail markers or subclasses (Zhou et al., 2023)

name: Thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN/RT) GABAergic neuron
morphology_summary: Neurons at gradient extremes show core-like vs shell-like organisation
ephys_summary: Electrophysiological properties co-vary with the transcriptomic gradient (integrative scRNA-seq plus electrophysiology, Li et al., 2020)
subtypes_noted: Continuous transcriptomic gradient with mutually exclusive Spp1 vs Ecel1 extremes; the two subpopulations connect differentially with first-order vs higher-order thalamic nuclei and their subnetworks affect sleep (Li et al., 2020); belongs to ABC class 12 HY GABA, shared with ZI, LGv and hypothalamus (Turner et al., 2025)

name: Ventral lateral geniculate nucleus / intergeniculate leaflet (LGv/IGL) GABAergic neuron
subtypes_noted: Derived from a Shh-responsive rostral thalamic (rTh.Pro / pTH-R) progenitor lineage distinct from most thalamic glutamatergic neurons (Govek et al., 2022); in ABC analyses LGv contributes to both class 12 HY GABA and class 20 MB GABA, suggesting heterogeneity (Turner et al., 2025); project to subcortical targets (Zhou et al., 2023). Fine subtype markers not given
